question: A client complains that taking a daily pill is too hard with her busy work schedule. What is a great recommendation to discuss?

options.A: Double the daily pill dose to make up for missed days
options.B: Scold the client for being irresponsible with her medication
options.C: Stop using all forms of contraception immediately
options.D: Discuss long-acting reversible options like implants or injectables

explanation: If daily pills are a struggle, methods like injectables or implants take away the stress of daily remembering while offering great protection.

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for terminal patients at home?

options.A: Finding a surgical cure for advanced cancer
options.B: Testing new experimental drugs that reverse aging
options.C: Isolating the patient from all family and friends
options.D: Providing comfort, symptom control, and preserving dignity

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and managing symptoms to ensure the highest possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: How do traditional gender expectations usually shape how teenagers behave?

options.A: By dictating how teens act, dress, and relate to others based on societal norms
options.B: By eliminating peer pressure during early adolescence
options.C: By ensuring all teenagers develop identical psychological coping mechanisms
options.D: By removing all biological differences between males and females

explanation: Exactly! Society often hands young people a script on how to dress, talk, and act depending on whether they are male or female.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally suffer a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Soak the finger in pure household bleach for ten minutes
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report it to the supervisor
options.C: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site immediately
options.D: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water

explanation: Stay calm! Wash the area right away with soap and running water to rinse away germs before they settle in.

question: What physical examination technique involves using a stethoscope to listen to internal body sounds?

options.A: Palpation
options.B: Inspection
options.C: Percussion
options.D: Auscultation

explanation: Auscultation is the act of listening to sounds within the body, such as the heart and lungs, using a stethoscope. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of an expectorant medication?

options.A: To kill bacterial infections in the lungs
options.B: To relax tightened muscles around the bronchi
options.C: To completely stop all coughing reflexes
options.D: To thin and loosen mucus in the airways

explanation: Spot on! Expectorants help loosen up thick, sticky phlegm so your body can cough it out much more easily.

question: Why do we strongly advise against using both hands to recap a needle?

options.A: It damages the sharpness of the needle tip
options.B: It makes the syringe difficult to read
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.D: It takes too much time during an emergency

explanation: Spot on! Trying to guide a cap back on with two hands is a recipe for poking your own finger. Safety rules are written in blood—let's protect those fingers!

question: Which type of depression tends to happen during specific times of the year, especially the cold winter months?

options.A: Seasonal affective disorder
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Persistent depressive disorder

explanation: You got it! Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) kicks in during certain seasons, usually when daylight gets shorter in the winter.

question: Why is Type O-negative blood considered the universal red cell donor?

options.A: The blood type is the most common found in humans
options.B: The red blood cells lack A, B, and Rh antigens
options.C: The red blood cells have no hemoglobin inside them
options.D: The plasma contains high levels of protective platelets

explanation: Because Type O-negative red blood cells carry none of the major antigens, recipient antibodies have nothing to react against. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main problem if a breastfeeding mother becomes severely dehydrated?

options.A: It turns the breast milk bright yellow
options.B: It stops the let-down reflex permanently
options.C: It permanently changes the infant's eye color
options.D: It can decrease breast milk supply

explanation: Since breast milk is mostly water, severe dehydration leaves the body with less fluid to make milk. Remember to keep a water bottle close by!

question: Why is the issue of consent particularly critical when discussing forced marriage?

options.A: Consent is only relevant in urban healthcare settings
options.B: Minors and coerced individuals cannot give free and informed agreement
options.C: Adults over 18 never experience forced marriage situations
options.D: Legal documents require parental signatures for all marriages

explanation: True consent requires maturity, capacity, and freedom from pressure, elements that are absent when external forces dictate a union. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: When is the right time to document a medication you just gave?

options.A: Before preparing the drug at the medication cart
options.B: At the very beginning of the nursing shift
options.C: At the end of the shift during the handover report
options.D: Immediately after giving the medication to the patient

explanation: Charting right away stops accidental double-dosing and keeps your records spotless. Great nursing habit to build early!

question: How can an unusually long fallopian tube affect the movement of an egg?

options.A: It slows down movement and can trap the egg inside
options.B: It stops the uterus from making female hormones
options.C: It completely stops the ovary from releasing eggs
options.D: It speeds up movement so much that the egg is destroyed

explanation: When a tube is extra long or twisted, the muscle movements are less efficient, making it easy for the slow-moving egg to get stuck. You've got this!

question: What is a safer alternative you can suggest to a new mother for easing perineal swelling instead of hot water?

options.A: Boiling steam directed continuously onto the surgical repair
options.B: Clean cold compresses or ice packs wrapped in a soft cloth
options.C: Total avoidance of any hygiene or washing for six weeks
options.D: Direct application of pure chemical bleach to numb the area

explanation: Ice packs are a nurse's best friend for fresh swelling! Cold numbs the pain and shrinks local blood vessels safely without burning or softening the tissues.

question: What is the frontline, life-saving medication for treating a patient in anaphylactic shock from a sting?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Amoxicillin
options.C: Hydrocortisone
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: You got it! Epinephrine is the gold standard because it quickly fixes dangerously low blood pressure and opens up closed airways.

question: Which animal serves as the natural home or reservoir for the Lassa virus?

options.A: Cow
options.B: Mosquito
options.C: Domestic cat
options.D: Multimammate rat

explanation: Exactly! The multimammate rat carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in its urine and droppings, which can accidentally contaminate our food.

question: Two family members disagree sharply on whether to pursue aggressive treatment for a failing relative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Facilitate a structured family meeting to let both parties voice concerns
options.B: Choose one family member at random to make all the final decisions
options.C: Tell the family members they are not allowed to visit anymore
options.D: Ignore the family conflict and follow only the primary doctor's orders

explanation: A structured meeting allows family members to express their viewpoints safely and helps the care team work toward consensus. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main reason pressure injuries (bedsores) develop?

options.A: Sustained mechanical pressure cutting off capillary blood flow
options.B: A sudden and severe deficiency in dietary vitamin A
options.C: An allergic reaction to harsh chemical cleaning soaps
options.D: Excessive exposure to natural ultraviolet sunlight

explanation: Spot on! When someone stays in one position too long, body weight pinches tiny blood vessels shut, starving the tissue of oxygen until it breaks down.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of orthostatic hypotension when a patient stands up suddenly?

options.A: Dizziness or lightheadedness
options.B: Sudden severe chest pain
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle tremors
options.D: Rapid elevation of body temperature

explanation: When blood pressure drops fast upon standing, the brain momentarily misses out on optimal blood flow, making the patient feel dizzy or lightheaded.

question: A maternity nurse ignores a fetal monitor beep because too many false alarms sounded earlier. What is this called?

options.A: Fixation error
options.B: Memory lapse
options.C: Confirmation bias
options.D: Alert fatigue

explanation: Well done! When machines beep too often for nothing, we get 'alert fatigue' and might sadly miss the one time the alarm is actually saving a life.

question: Why is you, the bedside nurse, so important in hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses write all national environmental health laws
options.B: Nurses are solely responsible for incinerator operations
options.C: Nurses supervise the daily clinical actions at the point of generation
options.D: Nurses purchase all hospital disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because you provide direct patient care every day, you control how waste is sorted and handled right at the bedside.

question: What is the biggest advantage of using qualitative methods like focus group discussions?

options.A: They eliminate the need to ever write a formal report
options.B: They provide deeper insight into cultural beliefs and local attitudes
options.C: They require no active participation from community members
options.D: They give exact numerical percentages of disease outbreaks

explanation: Numbers are great, but talking to people helps you understand the "why" behind their health habits and cultural beliefs!

question: What is the final goal of the complement cascade when attacking a bacterium?

options.A: Thickening of the local epithelial basement membrane
options.B: Production of specific IgE antibodies against the bacterial wall
options.C: Maturation of naive T-cells into active helper cells
options.D: Formation of a membrane attack complex that lyses the cell

explanation: You got it! The complement system builds a 'membrane attack complex' that drills holes in the germ until it bursts (lyses).

question: A nurse needs to give an IM vaccine to a healthy adult. Which site is the most appropriate choice?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Abdomen
options.C: Dorsogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: The deltoid muscle is easily accessible and standard for routine adult vaccinations like tetanus or influenza. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does the uterus typically feel when assessing a patient with puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Soft, boggy, tender, and larger than expected for the postpartum day
options.B: Displaced entirely to the left side with no tenderness
options.C: Firm, contracted, non-tender, and well below the umbilicus
options.D: Completely rigid like a board with absent bowel sounds

explanation: Infection slows down normal uterine shrinking (involution). Instead of feeling firm, a septic uterus often feels soft, bulky, and painful when you touch it.

question: A patient asks what happens to sperm immediately after they are created in the seminiferous tubules. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: They travel to the epididymis to mature.
options.B: They enter the prostate gland for activation.
options.C: They mix with urine in the urinary bladder.
options.D: They travel directly out through the penile skin.

explanation: After leaving the seminiferous tubules, sperm move into the duct system and head directly into the epididymis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using medicine for glaucoma?

options.A: To lower pressure inside the eye and protect the optic nerve
options.B: To increase blood flow directly to the retina and lens
options.C: To cure bacterial infections in the cornea
options.D: To widen the pupil and improve night vision

explanation: You've got this! In glaucoma, fluid builds up and creates pressure. Our main goal is to relieve that pressure so the delicate optic nerve stays safe from damage.

question: Which of these is a MISTAKE when getting a patient ready for a digital blood pressure check?

options.A: Making sure both of the patient's feet are flat on the floor
options.B: Asking the patient to stay quiet while the machine runs
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep a thick sweater on with the cuff rolled over it
options.D: Ensuring the patient rests quietly for five minutes beforehand

explanation: Always put the cuff directly on bare skin! Thick clothing or tight rolling can pinch the arm and mess up your numbers.

question: How would you best describe organizational culture in a hospital?

options.A: The official printed employee handbook issued at hiring
options.B: The shared values, beliefs, and unwritten rules of a workplace
options.C: The physical layout and architectural design of the building
options.D: The total annual financial revenue generated by the facility

explanation: Culture is the 'personality' of the ward—the unwritten habits, attitudes, and vibe shared by the healthcare team ("this is how we do things around here").

question: Where do adult Ascaris worms love to live inside the human body?

options.A: The small intestine
options.B: The bloodstream
options.C: The large intestine
options.D: The liver and bile ducts

explanation: Adult roundworms settle comfortably in the small intestine, where they hang out, feed, and lay eggs.

question: What role do abnormal proteins play in degenerative neurological disorders?

options.A: They protect neurons from oxidative stress
options.B: They form harmful clumps that disrupt cell function
options.C: They speed up normal electrical signals
options.D: They help repair damaged nerve pathways

explanation: Proteins that fold incorrectly build up inside or around nerve cells, interfering with normal operations and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which of these practices is NOT part of safe umbilical cord care taught by nurses?

options.A: Applying animal dung to stop bleeding
options.B: Using a sterile blade to cut the cord
options.C: Washing hands thoroughly before handling the cord
options.D: Keeping the cord stump dry and uncovered

explanation: Spot on! Putting things like animal dung or ash on the cord introduces tetanus spores and must always be avoided.

question: If a pregnant mum temporarily eats less protein, what does the placenta do to protect the baby?

options.A: The placenta actively pumps amino acids to the fetus, maintaining its supply.
options.B: Amino acids turn into glucose inside the placenta.
options.C: The fetus stops growing entirely until the mother eats more meat.
options.D: Fetal amino acid levels drop immediately to match the mother's level.

explanation: Clever placenta! Even if mum's intake dips, active transport lets the placenta push extra amino acids over to keep the baby well-nourished.

question: Why must an endotracheal tube with an inflated cuff be placed in an unconscious patient before gastric lavage?

options.A: To keep the patient's mouth open wide during tube insertion
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the lavage fluid
options.C: To deliver extra oxygen straight to the stomach lining
options.D: To protect the airway and stop fluid from entering the lungs

explanation: Unconscious patients lose their protective swallowing and gag reflexes, so a cuffed airway tube creates a physical barrier against aspiration of stomach washings. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h4)

question: Why is drinking plenty of water especially critical for a nursing mother?

options.A: Lactation permanently increases core body temperature
options.B: Nursing mothers completely stop feeling thirsty
options.C: Milk production requires extra sodium from blood
options.D: Breast milk is composed mostly of water

explanation: Spot on! Since breast milk is mostly water, nursing mums need extra fluids to keep up their milk supply and stay hydrated.

question: Which patient position is standard for examining a vulval cyst?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Lithotomy position
options.C: High Fowler position
options.D: Prone position

explanation: The lithotomy position (lying on the back with legs raised in stirrups) gives the best view and access for examining the external female genitalia safely.

question: Why don't standard painkillers like ibuprofen work well for severe nerve pain?

options.A: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs only work when applied directly to the skin
options.B: Ibuprofen cannot cross the blood-brain barrier under any circumstances
options.C: Pain receptors in the peripheral nerves are completely immune to chemical blockers
options.D: Neuropathic pain is caused by abnormal nerve firing rather than general tissue inflammation

explanation: Ibuprofen fights swelling and tissue inflammation, but nerve pain comes from electrical misfires in the pathway itself. Different problem, different solution!

question: What serious long-term problem can happen if severe, chronic anaemia is ignored?

options.A: Heart failure
options.B: Bone softening
options.C: Liver cirrhosis
options.D: Kidney stones

explanation: If the heart is forced to pump extra fast for months or years to move oxygen-poor blood, the heart muscle eventually gets exhausted and begins to fail.

question: Which sign tells you a patient has severe malaria instead of just uncomplicated malaria?

options.A: Impaired consciousness or coma
options.B: Loss of appetite
options.C: Mild intermittent headache
options.D: Low-grade joint pain

explanation: Spot on! Any sign of confusion, extreme weakness, or coma (cerebral malaria) means it's an emergency needing immediate inpatient care.

question: Why is community engagement a crucial part of a nurse's role in implementing PHC in Nigeria?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to work inside physical clinic buildings
options.B: It forces villagers to obey nursing orders without asking questions
options.C: It ensures health programs are culturally accepted and supported by local leaders
options.D: It eliminates the need for any government funding or medical supplies

explanation: When local leaders and community members are involved, they embrace health initiatives, leading to long-term success. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)

question: Why do premature babies often have trouble getting their ductus arteriosus to close?

options.A: The umbilical cord was left unclamped for too long after delivery
options.B: Their tissues are more sensitive to prostaglandins and have lower blood oxygen levels
options.C: Their liver produces excessive amounts of bile that block circulation
options.D: Their left atrium has too much pressure compared to the right atrium

explanation: You're learning fast! Preterm babies often have immature lungs (meaning less oxygen) and higher levels of natural chemicals that keep that shortcut vessel open.

question: Which type of transport needs cellular energy (ATP) to move nutrients against a concentration gradient?

options.A: Simple diffusion
options.B: Osmosis
options.C: Facilitated diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Spot on! When the body needs to push substances 'uphill' against a gradient, it has to spend energy (ATP)—hence the name active transport.

question: Why is the primary survey performed in a strict ABCDE order?

options.A: To make patient charting faster for the nursing staff
options.B: Because it is required by hospital administrative policy
options.C: To prevent the doctor from entering the room too early
options.D: To address the most life-threatening conditions first

explanation: The framework prioritizes vital body systems so that airway and breathing issues are resolved before moving to less urgent checks. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h2)

question: How is general hospital waste different from infectious waste?

options.A: Infectious waste is always heavier than general waste boxes
options.B: General waste requires special incineration before leaving the ward
options.C: General waste is non-hazardous and similar to normal household trash
options.D: Infectious waste comes only from the hospital kitchen

explanation: Exactly! General waste has no contamination risk (like empty paper packaging), unlike infectious items that carry pathogens.

question: Who are considered key stakeholders in community mobilisation?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.B: Pharmaceutical company owners only
options.C: Patients admitted to distant urban hospitals
options.D: Only foreign aid workers from abroad

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are influential figures who help guide community opinions and behaviours. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: A patient with hearing loss is struggling to catch your discharge instructions. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask a family member to take over all patient care responsibilities
options.B: Face the patient directly and speak in a clear, moderate tone
options.C: Shout loudly from across the room so they can hear better
options.D: Stop talking and write everything down in complex medical terms

explanation: Spot on! Facing them lets them see your face and lip-read, which makes understanding much easier.

question: What is the medical definition of a fracture?

options.A: A break in the continuity of a bone
options.B: An inflammation of the bone marrow
options.C: A complete tearing of a ligament
options.D: The stretching of a skeletal muscle

explanation: A fracture simply means the normal structure of the bone has been broken or cracked by an outside force or disease process. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.A: To accurately document characteristics of a population or situation
options.B: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical procedure
options.C: To prove that variable A causes a change in variable B
options.D: To compare two different patient groups after an intervention

explanation: Great job! Descriptive studies are all about painting a clear picture of what is going on right now, without needing to dig into the 'why' or 'how'.

question: What is the standard test used to check for a strep throat infection?

options.A: Sputum Gram stain
options.B: Throat swab culture
options.C: Peak flow measurement
options.D: Chest radiography

explanation: Correct! A quick swab of the back of the throat helps us check if streptococcus bacteria are causing the trouble.

question: Which tool is most commonly used for quick community screening of acute malnutrition in young children?

options.A: Basal metabolic rate calculation
options.B: Serum albumin concentration test
options.C: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
options.D: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference

explanation: The MUAC tape is lightweight, super fast, and amazing for field screening where fancy equipment isn't around.

question: What does it mean when a patient is in a positive energy balance?

options.A: Caloric expenditure is greater than caloric intake
options.B: Total body weight remains completely unchanging
options.C: Caloric intake and expenditure are perfectly equal
options.D: Caloric intake is greater than caloric expenditure

explanation: When you take in more food energy than your body burns, the extra energy is stored. That's a positive energy balance!

question: A patient comes in with sudden, severe eye pain, headache, vomiting, and seeing rainbow halos around lights. What should you suspect?

options.A: Simple presbyopia
options.B: Open-angle glaucoma
options.C: Closed-angle glaucoma
options.D: Allergic conjunctivitis

explanation: When eye drainage suddenly gets completely blocked, pressure spikes fast. This causes intense pain, nausea, and blurry rainbow halos around lights!

question: What does a nurse typically see during an otoscopic exam of a patient with acute ear infection (otitis media)?

options.A: A clear, translucent eardrum with a sharp cone of light
options.B: A dark perforated hole with dry flaky skin inside the canal
options.C: A bulging, bright red tympanic membrane with obscured landmarks
options.D: A completely pale, flat membrane with prominent bone outlines

explanation: When pus builds up behind the eardrum from an infection, it pushes the drum outward and turns it very red, hiding the normal landmarks.

question: Why does a crashing patient make standard IV drug delivery so difficult?

options.A: The skin becomes too thick for any needle to pierce
options.B: The blood begins to flow backward toward the feet
options.C: Emergency drugs are blocked by the skin's natural oil barrier
options.D: Peripheral veins flatten and collapse, making them hard to cannulate

explanation: When blood pressure drops severely, peripheral veins empty out and flatten. This makes slipping an IV cannula in super tough during an emergency!

question: Which device is commonly managed by modern critical care nurses to support kidney function?

options.A: Automated external pacemaker for heart block
options.B: Negative-pressure iron lung for breathing
options.C: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) machine
options.D: Intra-aortic balloon pump for cardiac support

explanation: CRRT is a specialized form of dialysis used in the ICU for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h6)

question: What immediate lab test must be done before giving a blood transfusion to a severely anaemic labor patient?

options.A: Complete metabolic panel
options.B: Clotting profile
options.C: Urinalysis culture
options.D: Type and crossmatch

explanation: Safety first! Typing and crossmatching ensure the donated blood matches the patient and won't cause a dangerous reaction.

question: A patient with locked-in syndrome can't speak or move, but blinks to answer questions. What is the most important first nursing action?

options.A: Assume the patient cannot understand instructions given in the room.
options.B: Establish a reliable communication system using eye movements.
options.C: Limit neurological checks to once every twenty-four hours.
options.D: Administer heavy sedation to reduce patient awareness.

explanation: Even though they can't speak, these patients are fully conscious! Setting up a simple blink-for-yes system brings them immense comfort and dignity.

question: What term is used when FGM is illegally performed inside a hospital or clinic by trained medical personnel?

options.A: Clinical harm reduction
options.B: Medicalization of FGM
options.C: Therapeutic intervention
options.D: Surgical modification

explanation: Spot on! 'Medicalization' means carrying out FGM in a health facility or by a health worker, which remains completely illegal and unethical.

question: Which physical sign is a classic warning flag that a patient might be experiencing abuse?

options.A: A surgical scar from an appendectomy performed years ago
options.B: Unexplained bruises in various stages of healing
options.C: Age-related thinning of the skin on the forearms
options.D: Symmetrical skin rashes caused by a new soap

explanation: You got it! Bruises looking fresh, yellow, and faded all at once usually point to repeated trauma over time, not a single clumsy accident.

question: Why does flying at high altitudes put patients at risk for low oxygen levels (hypoxia)?

options.A: The barometric pressure drops, reducing available oxygen levels
options.B: Cold cabin temperatures destroy red blood cells
options.C: The aircraft engines consume all the oxygen in the cabin
options.D: Patients stop breathing naturally due to engine noise

explanation: You got it! As you go higher up, atmospheric pressure drops, making it harder for oxygen to pass into the lungs. That's why cabin oxygen monitoring is so crucial.

question: A patient at 28 weeks reports sharp, regular tummy pains and a watery vaginal discharge. What should you suspect?

options.A: Typical pregnancy-related constipation
options.B: Normal round ligament stretching
options.C: Preterm labor or rupture of membranes
options.D: Benign nighttime leg cramps

explanation: Regular pain and fluid leakage before full term are signs of preterm labor or water breaking, which needs immediate evaluation. Excellent clinical judgment!

question: A patient has a stroke affecting the left frontal lobe. As a nurse, what sign might you notice?

options.A: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.B: Complete blindness in the left eye
options.C: Difficulty with voluntary movement on the right side
options.D: Inability to recognize familiar faces

explanation: The frontal lobe handles movement. Because brain pathways cross over, the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body!

question: Why do we quickly set up large-bore IV lines for a woman experiencing heavy postpartum bleeding?

options.A: To make it easier to administer oral painkillers and antibiotics
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving her limbs around too much
options.C: To measure the exact temperature of blood flowing through the veins
options.D: To allow rapid infusion of emergency fluids and blood replacement

explanation: Big veins and wide needles let IV fluids and blood rush in fast to fight off shock when a mother is bleeding out. Every second counts!

question: Which dietary habit is most likely to trigger a painful gout flare?

options.A: Consuming large amounts of fresh leafy green vegetables
options.B: Eating heavy portions of red meat and drinking beer
options.C: Using low-sodium table salt on regular home-cooked meals
options.D: Drinking several glasses of plain water throughout the day

explanation: You've got this! Red meat and alcohol (especially beer) are high in purines, which spike uric acid levels and make it harder for the kidneys to clear them.

question: What must a nurse do immediately after wiping a medication vial rubber top with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Allow the alcohol to dry completely before piercing
options.B: Blow on the rubber top to dry it fast
options.C: Insert the needle immediately while it is wet
options.D: Rinse the top with sterile tap water

explanation: Giving the alcohol time to air dry ensures proper disinfection of the rubber stopper surface. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which Christian group often eats a plant-based diet and avoids pork?

options.A: Roman Catholics
options.B: Seventh-day Adventists
options.C: Pentecostal believers
options.D: Eastern Orthodox

explanation: Seventh-day Adventists often choose vegetarianism and avoid pork because they view the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit. You'll likely see this in clinical practice!

question: What are the small, yellowish deposits that build up under the retina in dry age-related macular degeneration called?

options.A: Melanin granules
options.B: Drusen
options.C: Aqueous humor
options.D: Crystalline proteins

explanation: Great work! Drusen are tiny fatty deposits that collect under the retina as we age. Finding them is a key sign of dry macular degeneration.

question: What makes postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) such a major emergency for a new mother?

options.A: Chronic infection of the urinary tract
options.B: Severe blood loss that can quickly cause death
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Sudden permanent loss of vision

explanation: Exactly. Postpartum hemorrhage means rapid, heavy bleeding after birth. If we don't replace the blood volume quickly, it can lead to severe shock and danger very fast.

question: What do we call those little pouch-like segments you see along the length of the colon?

options.A: Haustra
options.B: Lacteals
options.C: Villi
options.D: Plicae circulares

explanation: Haustra are the cute little pocket formations on the colon created by its muscle bands. You're building solid anatomy knowledge!

question: How do standard clinical guidelines across a health network help patients?

options.A: It guarantees consistent quality of care regardless of which facility the patient visits
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing side effects from contraceptives
options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries without physician supervision
options.D: It reduces the cost of prescription medications to zero for all citizens

explanation: Well done! Shared guidelines mean a patient gets the same safe, top-notch care whether they walk into a rural health post or a city hospital.

question: What term is used to measure the amount of tracer absorbed in a specific spot on a PET scan?

options.A: Systemic Urine Volume
options.B: Standardized Uptake Value
options.C: Specific Ultrasound Velocity
options.D: Serum Utilization Variable

explanation: You got it! Radiologists use the Standardized Uptake Value (SUV) as a handy number to measure just how much tracer activity is happening in a specific tissue.

question: How should a nurse touch a newly applied plaster cast while it is still wet?

options.A: With the palms of the hands to avoid indentations
options.B: With a heating pad wrapped tightly around it
options.C: With rigid metal clamps for support
options.D: With the fingertips to check for soft spots

explanation: Always use your palms! Using your fingertips can leave deep dents in wet plaster, which press into the skin and cause painful sores.

question: Which germ causes oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Oral thrush is a fungal infection that happens when Candida albicans grows a bit too much in the mouth.

question: A client wants a birth control method that lasts for several years but can easily be removed if she decides to have another baby later. What type of method is this?

options.A: Permanent surgical sterilization
options.B: Long-acting reversible contraceptives
options.C: Natural calendar rhythm methods
options.D: Short-acting oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Correct! Long-acting reversible contraceptives (like IUDs and implants) give years of steady protection, but a nurse can take them out anytime the client is ready for pregnancy.

question: A patient who had a barium swallow two days ago reports no bowel movement, abdominal cramping, and bloating. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Immediate healing of an esophageal ulcer
options.B: A normal reaction to fasting before the test
options.C: Rapid absorption of contrast into the blood
options.D: Barium impaction leading to constipation

explanation: Barium dries out inside the large intestine, making constipation and impaction a major post-procedure risk if fluids and laxatives are not used. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h7)

question: A patient is taking oral iron pills. What advice should you give them to help their body absorb the iron better?

options.A: Take the supplement with vitamin C or orange juice
options.B: Crush the pills and mix them into a yogurt meal
options.C: Swallow the tablets immediately after drinking a glass of milk
options.D: Take the medication right before going to sleep at night

explanation: Vitamin C is iron's best friend! It creates an acidic environment in the stomach that helps the body absorb oral iron much more effectively.

question: What is the secret behind why Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) works so well?

options.A: Water absorption is stimulated by adding high amounts of sugar
options.B: Sodium and glucose transport together, pulling water into the body
options.C: Glucose completely paralyzes the nerves that cause bowel spasms
options.D: Sodium creates a thick barrier that blocks toxins from entering

explanation: Sodium and glucose team up in the gut wall. Even when you have diarrhoea, this special transport team helps pull water right back into your body.

question: When you are taking a family health history, which group of relatives should you focus on first?

options.A: Neighbors living in the same community
options.B: Colleagues and close personal friends
options.C: First-degree relatives like parents and siblings
options.D: Distant cousins and second-degree relatives

explanation: You nailed it! Parents, brothers, and sisters share the closest genetic traits with your patient, so their medical history matters most.

question: A nurse wants to address high salt intake in a local market. What should be the very first step?

options.A: Engage market vendors in a discussion about how they view salt use in local foods
options.B: Ban the sale of heavily salted processed snacks within the market stalls
options.C: Organize a mandatory lecture hall seminar for all registered market traders
options.D: Distribute brightly coloured pamphlets detailing the dangers of hypertension

explanation: Brilliant! True nursing care starts with listening. Always involve the community and understand their perspective before trying to change their habits.

question: Which metabolic process involves building complex body tissues from simpler substances?

options.A: Excretion
options.B: Catabolism
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Digestion

explanation: Think of 'Anabolism' as adding blocks to build things up—like turning simple amino acids into strong muscles.

question: During pin site care, why should you avoid scrubbing away dried crusts around the pins?

options.A: Crusts are needed to hold the metal pin tightly in place
options.B: Crusts act as a protective barrier against bacteria
options.C: Scrubbing crusts will cause the traction weights to fall off
options.D: Dried blood keeps the patient's scalp warm and dry

explanation: Hands off those crusts! They actually act like a natural little shield protecting the healing skin underneath from germs.

question: In the ward, what do we mean by an 'adverse event'?

options.A: Harm caused by medical management rather than the disease
options.B: An unavoidable symptom of a natural disease process
options.C: Any emotional stress a patient feels before surgery
options.D: A patient refusing to take prescribed hospital medications

explanation: Spot on! An adverse event means the patient got hurt because of the care or treatment given, not because of their sickness itself. You'll master these safety terms in no time!

question: Which of these is a main source of laboratory-based surveillance data?

options.A: Confirmation of specific germs and drug resistance patterns
options.B: Commercial market prices for staple foods
options.C: Records of primary school student attendance
options.D: Daily weather forecasts and rainfall measurements

explanation: The lab tells us the exact culprit making people sick and whether standard drugs can fight it off or if the germ is resistant.

question: Why do persons with physical disabilities often struggle to get loans from regular commercial banks?

options.A: Government laws require all loans to be interest-free
options.B: Microfinance banks are legally banned from helping them
options.C: Banks often view disability as a high credit risk and demand strict collateral
options.D: Commercial banks automatically pay all medical bills

explanation: Traditional lenders can be rigid and prejudiced, making it difficult for disabled entrepreneurs to get startup money without strong guarantees.

question: Which of these is NOT the right way to handle workplace violence in a hospital?

options.A: Using de-escalation techniques to calm an agitated patient
options.B: Ensuring an easy exit route is available during a patient interview
options.C: Accepting physical abuse quietly because it is part of the job
options.D: Reporting all threatening incidents to hospital security and management

explanation: Violence is never part of the job description. If someone threatens or abuses you, report it and use your hospital's security protocols immediately.

question: Pick's disease mainly affects which areas of the brain first?

options.A: Frontal and temporal lobes
options.B: Occipital and parietal lobes
options.C: Thalamus and hypothalamus
options.D: Cerebellum and brainstem

explanation: Pick's disease zeroes in on the frontal and temporal parts of the brain, which handle our personality, behavior, and language. Spotting this early helps you understand why patients act differently long before memory issues start!

question: Why do fertility specialists always insist on evaluating both partners during a fertility workup?

options.A: Because female infertility is extremely rare compared to male causes
options.B: To prove insurance coverage before starting expensive procedures
options.C: To rule out genetic disorders in unrelated family members
options.D: Because male and female factors contribute almost equally to infertility

explanation: That's right! Fertility struggles happen pretty evenly across both partners, so testing both saves time and heartache. Brilliant thinking!

question: What is the main goal when caring for a patient with a secondary metastatic tumour in the heart?

options.A: Palliative care and managing symptoms while treating the primary cancer source
options.B: Preventing the patient from ever moving their arms or legs
options.C: Permanent replacement of all four heart valves with artificial ones
options.D: Complete surgical cure of the heart muscle using a heart transplant

explanation: When cancer has spread from elsewhere, the focus shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and treating the original cancer source. Compassionate nursing at its best!

question: A newborn was successfully resuscitated and is now stable. Which nursing action is NOT correct for their ongoing care?

options.A: Allowing the infant to experience untreated mild hypothermia to rest
options.B: Tracking oxygen saturations against target ranges
options.C: Observing for signs of neurological irritability
options.D: Monitoring blood glucose levels regularly

explanation: Getting too cold makes a baby use up more oxygen and makes acid build up in their blood. We always work hard to keep their body temperature normal!

question: Why can taking too many fat-soluble vitamins become dangerous?

options.A: All vitamins contain high levels of dangerous dietary sodium
options.B: Excess vitamins immediately turn into stored body fat
options.C: High vitamin levels completely stop normal digestion
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity

explanation: Unlike water-soluble vitamins that wash right out, fat-soluble ones get stored in body tissues and can build up to harmful levels.

question: When does the immediate puerperium period happen?

options.A: Between the second and sixth week
options.B: Before the placenta is delivered
options.C: The first 24 hours after delivery
options.D: The entire first week after birth

explanation: Spot on! The immediate puerperium covers the first 24 hours post-delivery. As nurses, we watch new mums closely during this window because the risk for heavy bleeding is at its highest.

question: Which of these measurements counts as an anthropometric assessment?

options.A: Respiratory depth
options.B: Heart rhythm
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Height and weight

explanation: Anthropometric measurements are simply body dimensions and size—like height, weight, and waist circumference. Easy peasy!

question: What makes the blood-brain barrier so tough for most drugs to cross?

options.A: Tightly joined capillary cells with no large pores
options.B: A thick outer layer of skull bone
options.C: Constant high-speed blood flow that washes drugs away
options.D: Enzymes in the blood that destroy drugs instantly

explanation: Unlike regular blood vessels that have tiny spaces for things to slip through, brain capillaries are locked together tightly to protect the brain.

question: Why shouldn't you give anti-bleeding (antihaemorrhagic) drugs to a patient who already has active blood clots?

options.A: It lowers their blood pressure too quickly
options.B: It stops the liver from making albumin
options.C: It prevents the kidneys from filtering urine
options.D: It can cause dangerous new clots in vital organs

explanation: If a patient is already forming unwanted clots, giving drugs that promote clotting is like pouring fuel on a fire—it can cause dangerous blockages!

question: What is a simple thing a nurse can do to build trust about injection safety?

options.A: Ask the doctor to perform all medication preparations
options.B: Show the sterile needle pack to the patient before opening it
options.C: Administer all injections behind a closed privacy curtain
options.D: Hide the syringe until the procedure is completely finished

explanation: Wonderful! Showing an unopened, sterile pack instantly reassures the patient that you take their safety seriously.

question: The neural tube, which forms the brain and spinal cord, develops from which germ layer?

options.A: Endoderm
options.B: Trophoblast
options.C: Mesoderm
options.D: Ectoderm

explanation: Since the nervous system links closely with the skin and outer structures, it comes right from the ectoderm layer. Excellent recall!

question: Why are proper body positioning and early splinting so important in burn rehab?

options.A: To prevent debilitating joint contractures caused by scar tightening
options.B: To maintain adequate arterial blood pressure in the extremities
options.C: To speed up the re-epithelialization of superficial donor sites
options.D: To stop the hypermetabolic energy expenditure phase early

explanation: Healing burn scars love to pull and tighten joints into awkward bends. Splints and good positioning keep patients stretched out and moving freely!

question: What is the biggest benefit of encouraging community participation in health programs?

options.A: It removes the need for trained professional nurses and doctors entirely
options.B: It allows the government to avoid spending any money on healthcare infrastructure
options.C: It shifts all legal liability for illness outbreaks onto local villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term sustainability of the programs

explanation: When a community feels 'this project is ours,' they will take care of it and keep it running long after outside help leaves.

question: A client who uses a three-monthly injectable contraceptive fails to show up on her due date. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Initiate a follow-up contact to check on her and reschedule
options.B: Assume she has moved away and close the clinic permanently
options.C: Wait patiently for two years before taking any action
options.D: Throw away her clinic file immediately to save space

explanation: Tracing defaulters helps find out why they missed their visit, offers counseling, and prevents method discontinuation gaps. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h6)

question: Four hours after a normal vaginal delivery, a mum hasn't peed yet, and her uterus feels soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is likely happening?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure caused by blood loss
options.B: A full bladder preventing the uterus from contracting
options.C: Normal postpartum diuresis filling the renal pelvis
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to low urine production

explanation: A full bladder acts like a roadblock, pushing the uterus out of place and stopping it from contracting properly. Always check the bladder if you notice a boggy uterus—it can prevent postpartum hemorrhage!

question: When is a nurse most likely to consider using the rectal route for a patient?

options.A: When the patient prefers a fast topical skin effect
options.B: When the patient needs a daily multivitamin tablet
options.C: When the patient cannot take medications by mouth
options.D: When the patient has a mild headache and can swallow

explanation: If oral intake is blocked due to vomiting, unconsciousness, or swallowing difficulties, the rectal route serves as a practical alternative. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does the small intestine release secretin into the bloodstream?

options.A: To neutralize incoming stomach acid with bicarbonate
options.B: To slow down the movement of food through the esophagus
options.C: To stop the liver from producing cholesterol
options.D: To trigger the immediate feeling of hunger

explanation: Secretin is released when acidic chyme arrives from the stomach. It calls for alkaline bicarbonate to protect your delicate intestinal lining—pretty smart teamwork by the body! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h2)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure thirty minutes after giving a blood pressure medication to see if it dropped into the normal range. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results after an intervention to see if goals were met is the definition of the evaluation phase. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: A nursing student observes a mother struggling to latch her newborn baby. What instruction should the nurse give first?

options.A: Wait until the baby cries loudly to ensure the mouth is open wide enough
options.B: Push the nipple forcefully into the center of the baby's closed mouth
options.C: Bring the baby's wide-open mouth to the breast, not the breast to the baby
options.D: Apply petroleum jelly to the nipple to help the baby slide on easier

explanation: Moving the baby toward the breast ensures a deep latch that includes a large portion of the lower areola, preventing nipple pain. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: When reading a Mantoux test, what part of the skin reaction do you actually measure?

options.A: The hard, raised area of tissue known as induration
options.B: The dark bruising caused by the needle puncture
options.C: The total diameter of visible surface redness
options.D: The size of the initial wheal left after the injection

explanation: Don't measure the redness! Feel for the edges of that firm, hard bump underneath (the induration)—that's what tells the real story. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h5)

question: What is the safest thing to do right after giving an injection with a disposable syringe?

options.A: Place the uncapped syringe on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Drop the entire syringe into a nearby sharps container
options.C: Recap the needle firmly using a two-handed technique
options.D: Break the needle off before disposal

explanation: Correct! To avoid accidental needle pricks, always drop the whole sharp device straight into a puncture-resistant container without trying to recap it.

question: Why must nurses adjust their teaching style when educating patients about blood health?

options.A: To prove that modern medicine is superior to local traditions
options.B: To match the patient's literacy level and cultural background
options.C: To make the education session finish much faster
options.D: To ensure the medical terms are as complex as possible

explanation: Clear, culturally sensitive communication ensures patients truly understand how to protect their health and follow prevention guidelines. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary role of effective communication in a primary health care setting?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written medical records
options.B: Reducing the cost of medical equipment
options.C: Building trust and ensuring treatment understanding
options.D: Speeding up the patient discharge process

explanation: Clear communication helps establish a strong nurse-patient relationship, which makes patients more likely to share accurate information and follow their care plans. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h1)

question: A patient with long-term chronic gastritis is most at risk for lacking which vitamin?

options.A: Vitamin C deficiency
options.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency
options.C: Calcium deficiency
options.D: Potassium deficiency

explanation: Exactly! When gastritis damages the stomach's parietal cells, you lose intrinsic factor, meaning your body can't absorb vitamin B12 like it should.

question: What is the primary purpose of drug legislation in nursing?

options.A: To increase the cost of essential medicines
options.B: Um, to reduce the workload of hospital pharmacists
options.C: To make medication administration slower
options.D: To protect the public and healthcare workers

explanation: Drug laws exist mainly to keep patients safe from harm and guide nurses on legal medication practices. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a bone marrow aspiration and a bone marrow biopsy?

options.A: Biopsy checks cell maturity, while aspiration checks bone strength
options.B: Biopsy uses arm veins, while aspiration uses the sternum
options.C: Aspiration needs general anaesthesia, but biopsy does not
options.D: Aspiration takes liquid, while a biopsy takes a solid piece of tissue

explanation: Think of aspiration as taking a fluid sample of the marrow, while a biopsy takes a tiny solid cylinder of bone and marrow to check its structure.

question: How is being 'hard of hearing' different from profound deafness?

options.A: Hard of hearing always requires immediate surgical intervention
options.B: Hard of hearing individuals retain some residual hearing capacity
options.C: Deafness is always caused by an infection in the outer ear
options.D: Deaf individuals can still understand whispered conversations easily

explanation: Patients who are hard of hearing still have some hearing left (residual hearing). This means devices like hearing aids can help them a lot!

question: What does the nutrition acronym RDA stand for?

options.A: Required Drug Amount
options.B: Regular Dietary Analysis
options.C: Rapid Daily Assessment
options.D: Recommended Dietary Allowance

explanation: RDA is the standard daily amount of a nutrient you need to keep nearly all healthy people thriving.

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

options.A: Biodegradable
options.B: Odorless
options.C: Flammable
options.D: Transparent

explanation: That's right! Materials that are flammable, corrosive, toxic, or reactive are flagged as hazardous and heavily regulated.

question: What is a major barrier that prevents teenagers from visiting clinics for contraceptives?

options.A: The high academic performance required to enter clinics
options.B: Mandatory free transport provided to all school children
options.C: A complete absence of any illness during adolescence
options.D: Fear of judgmental staff and lack of confidentiality

explanation: Many teens avoid clinics because they fear being scolded by healthcare workers or having their visits reported to their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: What is the best way to stop a nasogastric tube from getting blocked?

options.A: Changing the tube to a smaller size every week
options.B: Adding cooking oil to every feed
options.C: Flushing it with warm water before and after feeds and drugs
options.D: Blowing air down the tube twice a shift

explanation: Regular water flushes wash away sticky food and medicine residue before they can dry up and clog your tube.

question: What is the main type of data collected in qualitative research?

options.A: Statistical percentages
options.B: Laboratory test values
options.C: Narrative text and words
options.D: Blood pressure readings

explanation: Quali-tative = Quality and stories! Instead of crunching numbers, it focuses on capturing human experiences through interviews, notes, and words.

question: What was the main problem with most ancient birth control methods?

options.A: They were too expensive for ordinary citizens to purchase
options.B: They were frequently toxic, unreliable, or completely ineffective
options.C: They required advanced surgical equipment available only to royalty
options.D: They relied on electronic monitoring of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Ancient remedies relied a lot on guesswork and folk traditions, which often meant they didn't work well and could even be unsafe.

question: During childbirth, how does infibulation primarily cause distress to the baby?

options.A: The placenta detaches early due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: The mother's blood pressure drops too low to feed the baby
options.C: Amniotic fluid turns toxic within the closed space
options.D: Rigid scar tissue obstructs delivery, causing prolonged pressure on the baby

explanation: Spot on! Tough scar tissue makes it hard for the baby to pass through, leading to prolonged labor and a lack of oxygen.

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?

options.A: Insisting that she must purchase organic foods to have a healthy baby
options.B: Suggesting affordable, locally available food alternatives that meet her nutritional needs
options.C: Skipping dietary counseling because poverty makes nutrition impossible to change
options.D: Telling her to buy expensive imported supplements from specialized pharmacies

explanation: Great nursing care is practical and real! Always guide patients toward nourishing, budget-friendly local foods they can actually access.

question: What hormone causes the rise in basal body temperature after ovulation?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone is a thermogenic hormone released after ovulation that slightly increases the basal body temperature. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h2)

question: What is the main job of drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) when treating erectile dysfunction?

options.A: Increasing red blood cell production
options.B: Lowering systemic body temperature
options.C: Relaxing the muscles in the bladder
options.D: Enhancing blood flow to penile tissues

explanation: Awesome! These meds relax smooth muscles so blood can flow easily into the penis when the patient is stimulated.

question: About how long are the intestines in an adult human body when fully stretched out?

options.A: Fifteen meters
options.B: Two meters
options.C: Nine meters
options.D: One meter

explanation: It sounds unbelievable because they fit inside our belly, but our intestines stretch to about nine meters long! You've got this.

question: How does losing access to school affect a young bride's future?

options.A: It makes her physically unable to speak clearly to healthcare workers
options.B: It limits her ability to earn money and understand basic health information
options.C: It forces her to move permanently to a foreign country
options.D: It guarantees she will develop severe bone disorders in old age

explanation: Well reasoned! Without education, she misses out on financial independence and health awareness, keeping her trapped in vulnerability.

question: What is the absolute lowest possible total score a patient can get on the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?
explanation: Since every section (eyes, verbal, motor) gives at least 1 point even if unresponsive, the lowest possible total is 3.

question: Family members demand resuscitation for a dying patient who has a valid Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) order. How should you respond?

options.A: Calmly explain the valid DNR order while comforting the family
options.B: Leave the house at once and call the police
options.C: Ignore the family and give high-dose emergency medications
options.D: Begin chest compressions immediately to keep the family happy

explanation: Well done! A valid DNR must be respected. Use a calm, reassuring voice to help grieving relatives understand the patient's documented wishes.

question: Which of these conditions means a client should definitely NOT take combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: History of deep vein thrombosis
options.B: History of simple ovarian cysts
options.C: Mild seasonal allergies
options.D: Controlled gestational diabetes

explanation: Spotting red flags is a key nursing skill! Estrogen increases the risk of blood clots, so a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a strict 'no-go' for combined pills.

question: What does a serum ferritin blood test tell the healthcare team?

options.A: Circulating blood sugar
options.B: Active vitamin B12 levels
options.C: Red blood cell lifespan
options.D: Stored iron reserves

explanation: Think of ferritin as the body's iron savings account. A serum ferritin test lets you see how much iron is safely tucked away in storage.

question: In a patient health history, what do we mean by the 'chief complaint'?

options.A: The primary reason the patient is seeking care, in their own words
options.B: The surgical history from the patient's childhood
options.C: The final medical diagnosis written by the attending physician
options.D: A complete list of every prescription medication the patient takes

explanation: Spot-on! The chief complaint is simply the main trouble or symptom that brought the patient to the clinic, written using what they tell you.

question: Which of these shows ethical financial management by a nurse leader?

options.A: Falsifying patient treatment records to increase insurance reimbursement claims
options.B: Accepting personal cash gifts from commercial medical supply vendors
options.C: Hiding budget overruns from executive leadership to avoid difficult questions
options.D: Accurately reporting staff hours and avoiding fraudulent billing practices

explanation: Honesty is everything in nursing. Accurately reporting hours and keeping bills transparent protects the profession and keeps patient trust strong.

question: Why might two patients given the exact same dose of a drug experience completely different effects?

options.A: Manufacturers change drug potencies randomly every single day
options.B: Patients always take their prescribed drugs at different times
options.C: Individual biological and environmental factors alter drug disposition
options.D: Hospital pharmacies always dispense different medication strengths

explanation: You'll see this a lot in the wards! Every patient has unique factors like age, diet, and organ function that change how their body handles medications. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a tele-triage nursing service?

options.A: Conducting mandatory annual physical fitness exams for workers
options.B: Performing emergency major surgeries over a video conference
options.C: Evaluating sudden symptoms and advising on the appropriate level of care
options.D: Dispensing free prescription drugs directly to callers via mail

explanation: Tele-triage involves assessing a caller's symptoms over the phone to guide them on where and how fast to seek medical attention. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why is keeping a good stock of uterotonic drugs critical in a PAC unit?

options.A: To prevent or treat severe uterine bleeding and hemorrhage
options.B: To reverse the side effects of general anesthesia
options.C: To speed up the return of normal ovulation cycles
options.D: To relieve severe lower abdominal cramping pain

explanation: Uterotonics like oxytocin or misoprostol make the uterine muscle contract, which is a lifesaver for stopping dangerous blood loss after evacuation.

question: Why is training in adolescent psychology helpful for nurses?

options.A: It guarantees higher government salaries
options.B: It allows nurses to prescribe adult psychiatric drugs
options.C: It replaces the need for physical examinations
options.D: It helps providers communicate effectively without personal biases

explanation: Correct! Good training helps us handle sensitive youth issues with empathy and professionalism, leaving personal judgment at the door.

question: Which management theory assumes that employees dislike work and must be tightly controlled?

options.A: Systems theory
options.B: Theory Y
options.C: Theory X
options.D: Virtue ethics

explanation: Theory X is the pessimistic view of workers—it assumes people are lazy, want to avoid responsibility, and need a strict boss watching their every move.

question: What is a classic sign that a patient developed a pneumothorax after a thoracentesis?

options.A: Swelling and redness around the patient's ankles
options.B: Sudden severe pain radiating down the left arm
options.C: Sudden shortness of breath and absent breath sounds on one side
options.D: A high fever with productive green sputum and chills

explanation: Great clinical eye! If air leaks into the chest, it causes the lung to pull away, leading to sudden trouble breathing and quiet breath sounds on that side.

question: Which cranial nerve controls the muscles for chewing and lets you feel sensations on your face?

options.A: Olfactory nerve
options.B: Hypoglossal nerve
options.C: Trochlear nerve
options.D: Trigeminal nerve

explanation: Cranial Nerve V (the trigeminal nerve) is responsible for feeling things on your face and helping you chew your food.

question: Why do patients with untreated diabetes sometimes experience rapid weight loss?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake flushes away all dietary nutrients
options.B: High blood sugar levels speed up the normal metabolic rate
options.C: Kidneys filter out solid food particles into the urine
options.D: The body breaks down stored fat and muscle for energy

explanation: When glucose can't enter the cells for fuel, the body panics and starts burning its own fat and muscle instead, causing sudden weight loss. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: What is considered the absolute best (gold standard) way to confirm a nasogastric tube is in the right spot?

options.A: Measuring the length of tubing left outside the nose
options.B: Listening for air sounds over the belly with a stethoscope
options.C: Checking for water drops inside the clear plastic tube
options.D: Abdominal X-ray

explanation: An X-ray gives us clear visual proof that the tip is sitting comfortably in the stomach before we start any feeding.

question: What is the main job of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To connect the central nervous system to the rest of the body
options.B: To produce vital brain chemicals
options.C: To store long-term memories in the brain
options.D: To protect the delicate spinal cord from physical injury

explanation: You got it! Think of the peripheral nervous system as the network of highways carrying messages back and forth between your brain/spinal cord and your limbs.

question: Why do we prefer feeding through a stomach tube rather than an IV drip when the patient's digestive system is working?

options.A: It keeps the gut healthy and stops bad bacteria from moving around
options.B: It is completely painless and requires no monitoring
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of aspiration
options.D: It takes only a few minutes to set up every morning

explanation: Using the normal digestive tract keeps the gut lining strong and stops dangerous bacteria from escaping into the bloodstream. You've got this!

question: What is the safest way to check a patient's identity before starting an IV?

options.A: Look at the medication chart resting on the bedside table
options.B: Ask the client what room they are currently staying in
options.C: Check the client's identification band using two unique identifiers
options.D: Call out the client's full name and wait for a head nod

explanation: Safety first! Always use two patient identifiers (like name and hospital number on the ID band) to make sure you are giving the right treatment to the right person.

question: Why is keeping the cuticle intact so important for your patient?

options.A: It gives the nail plate its hard texture
options.B: It controls how fast the nail grows daily
options.C: It supplies the blood flow to the nail bed
options.D: It acts as a seal against bacteria and moisture

explanation: You've got this! Think of the cuticle as a natural bodyguard. It seals out water and germs so they don't slip under the skin and cause infection.

question: Which of these is NOT a positive sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Active movement felt by the examiner
options.B: Amenorrhea for two months
options.C: Fetal heartbeat heard on Doppler
options.D: Fetus visible on an ultrasound scan

explanation: Missing a period is a presumptive sign, not a positive one, because stress or illness can also stop menstruation. Only concrete proof like a heartbeat or scan is positive!

question: Why is proper handling and safe transport of laboratory specimens crucial during an outbreak?

options.A: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements in the hospital
options.B: To ensure the laboratory results are ready within five minutes
options.C: To prevent accidental exposure of staff and sample contamination
options.D: To keep the cost of running diagnostic tests as low as possible

explanation: Infectious samples carry live pathogens that can infect handlers or ruin the test if mishandled or contaminated along the way. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: A ward manager in a public hospital faces severe supply shortages and staff burnout. What is the best way to handle this leadership challenge?

options.A: Waiting passively for central government authorities to fix all facility problems
options.B: Strictly punishing staff members whenever minor supply miscounts occur
options.C: Using adaptive authority to build consensus, mentor staff, and solve problems creatively
options.D: Ignoring hospital protocols entirely and letting junior nurses run the ward

explanation: When resources are tight, great leaders don't just punish—they lean on teamwork, mentor each other, and find creative local solutions to keep caring for patients.

question: Why must public health programs keep working even after a disease is 'eliminated' in a specific region?

options.A: To keep the pharmaceutical companies funded
options.B: Because local health workers need ongoing employment
options.C: Because the pathogen can spontaneously reform locally
options.D: To prevent re-introduction of the pathogen from other areas

explanation: Spot on! Elimination just means it's gone locally. Since it still exists in other parts of the world, travelers can easily bring it back if we drop our guard.

question: Under current Nigerian laws, when is a pregnancy termination generally allowed?

options.A: If the pregnancy results from consensual teenage dating
options.B: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases during the first trimester
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it in writing

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian laws are quite strict and typically permit abortion only when carrying the pregnancy to term puts the mother's life in danger.

question: What is the best eating strategy for a patient dealing with severe nausea and poor appetite?

options.A: Encouraging three large, heavy meals to catch up on lost calories
options.B: Forcing the patient to finish everything on a large dinner plate
options.C: Withholding all food until appetite returns spontaneously
options.D: Serving small, frequent nutrient-dense meals throughout the day

explanation: Huge meals can make a nauseous patient feel worse. Small, tasty bites spaced through the day are much easier to manage!

question: Which complication is most directly prevented by flushing a gastrostomy tube regularly?

options.A: Allergic skin reactions to medical tape
options.B: Involuntary weight loss and muscle wasting
options.C: Severe lung infection caused by fluid aspiration
options.D: Tube occlusion from formula or pill residue

explanation: Regular water flushes clear out sticky nutritional formula and crushed medication particles before they dry and block the lumen. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why would you pass a nasogastric (NG) tube for a patient dealing with a bowel obstruction?

options.A: Gastric decompression and drainage
options.B: Measuring exact daily urine output
options.C: Continuous monitoring of blood pressure
options.D: Intravenous fluid replacement therapy

explanation: When the bowel is blocked, nothing moves down. An NG tube helps drain out built-up gas and fluid so the patient's stomach feels much relieved! Great job keeping this clinical logic clear.

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing hereditary conditions?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to speak directly with patients
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members for every patient
options.C: No single profession has all the skills needed to address complex genetic and social needs
options.D: It ensures that laboratory scientists make all final clinical decisions

explanation: Hereditary conditions involve medical, emotional, and social challenges that require diverse expertise from multiple healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: Which cultural factor often contributes to severe maternal health issues in rural areas?

options.A: Excessive use of modern antenatal care clinics in the first trimester
options.B: Reliance on unskilled traditional attendants for complicated deliveries
options.C: Early mandatory retirement for women of childbearing age
options.D: Over-consumption of iron-rich foods due to local cultural taboos

explanation: When women rely on birth attendants who cannot manage emergencies, getting specialized medical care is dangerously delayed. Community health education helps bridge this gap!

question: What must you do if an unsterile object accidentally touches your sterile field while setting up?

options.A: Throw away the whole field and set up a fresh sterile kit.
options.B: Spray antiseptic over the area and wait two minutes.
options.C: Wipe the spot with alcohol and keep going.
options.D: Ignore it if the object looked clean enough.

explanation: Safety first! If a sterile field is touched by something unsterile, its clean status is broken and you have to start fresh. Better safe than sorry in infection control.

question: When you accidentally touch something very hot and pull your hand away instantly, which nerve endings feel that pain?

options.A: Ruffini endings
options.B: Pacinian corpuscles
options.C: Free nerve endings
options.D: Meissner's corpuscles

explanation: Well done! Free nerve endings reach up into the skin to act as our alarm system for pain and temperature changes.

question: Why is it important to involve local community assets during resource mobilization?

options.A: Government policy forbids spending money on outside contractors
options.B: Local villagers are the only people legally allowed to handle medical drugs
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to write any project reports
options.D: It builds local ownership and reduces complete reliance on external funding

explanation: Using local resources ensures the community values the project and can sustain it even if external donors leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the main difference between an 'illness' and a 'disease'?

options.A: Disease can be cured by nursing care, but illness requires surgery.
options.B: Illness is a subjective feeling of being unwell, while disease is a physical alteration in body function.
options.C: Illness is diagnosed by laboratory tests, while disease is felt by the patient.
options.D: Illness only affects mental stability, whereas disease strictly affects organs.

explanation: Think of it this way: disease is the actual physical problem happening inside the body, while illness is how the patient actually experiences and feels that problem.

question: What main trigger causes the kidneys to release erythropoietin in patients with chronic lung disease?

options.A: High levels of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: Increased blood pressure in the right atrium
options.C: Persistent low blood oxygen levels
options.D: Reduced production of pulmonary surfactant

explanation: Brilliant! When the kidneys sense low oxygen (hypoxemia) over a long time, they release erythropoietin to tell the bone marrow to make more red blood cells. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h7)

question: An elderly patient leaks small amounts of liquid stool daily. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Bacterial food poisoning
options.B: Severe ulcerative colitis flare
options.C: Normal recovery from constipation
options.D: Fecal impaction with overflow

explanation: Liquid stool often leaks around a hard, impacted blockage in the rectum, which can trick people into thinking it is diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of failing to record items taken from the ward inventory?

options.A: The medications on the shelf will expire much faster than normal
options.B: The hospital will automatically order double the amount needed
options.C: Patients will recover faster because fewer drugs are logged
options.D: Stock counts will not match actual inventory, causing unexpected shortages

explanation: Unrecorded items create hidden inventory gaps, making reorder calculations inaccurate and leading to sudden stockouts. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: A high level of uric acid in the blood is a major clue for doctors diagnosing which condition?

options.A: Bone fracture
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Muscle atrophy
options.D: Gout

explanation: Gout happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints. Checking blood uric acid is a fast way to spot it!

question: Which of these best describes emotional abuse?

options.A: Withholding financial resources to pay for basic food items
options.B: Constant insults and public humiliation intended to destroy self-esteem
options.C: Denying access to emergency medical care during an illness
options.D: The intentional use of physical force to cause bodily injury

explanation: Great job! Emotional abuse hits a person's mental peace through constant insults, shaming, and public humiliation to break down their confidence.

question: Which factor contributes heavily to nursing staff shortages in many Nigerian health units?

options.A: Mandatory retirement at age twenty-five
options.B: The migration of experienced nurses abroad
options.C: Strict laws banning hospital employment
options.D: A complete lack of nursing training schools

explanation: You're spot on. The 'japa' wave has caused many skilled nurses to move abroad for better opportunities, leaving local units short-staffed.
