question: Why do community health nurses pay special attention to vulnerable populations?

options.A: They represent the majority of patients in private clinics
options.B: They are the only group legally mandated to receive free healthcare
options.C: They face higher risks for poor health outcomes due to limited resources
options.D: They always live within walking distance of primary health centers

explanation: Vulnerable groups often struggle to get money, food, or medical care, making them much more likely to fall sick. As nurses, they are our priority!

question: What is the most immediate danger when someone has severe, nonstop vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: Upper airway obstruction
options.B: Chronic hair loss
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: Permanent hearing impairment

explanation: Losing water and electrolytes too fast causes blood pressure to crash, which can quickly become life-threatening if not treated.

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest amount of energy per gram?

options.A: Carbohydrate
options.B: Protein
options.C: Fat
options.D: Water

explanation: Fats provide nine calories per gram, which is more than double the energy density found in carbohydrates or proteins. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h3)

question: What is one of the most common ways nurses accidentally get needle-stick injuries on duty?

options.A: Transporting bins during morning shift changes
options.B: Recapping used injection needles
options.C: Using plastic syringes instead of glass
options.D: Emptying safety boxes when they are full

explanation: Spot on. Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle puts your fingers right in the line of fire. Best practice? Never recap needles!

question: In health informatics, what does the abbreviation CPOE stand for?

options.A: Certified Practical Operations Expert
options.B: Computerized Provider Order Entry
options.C: Central Pharmacy Order Exchange
options.D: Clinical Patient Online Evaluation

explanation: CPOE is just the digital system doctors and other providers use to type their orders directly into the computer network.

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.A: Universal preference for large families exceeding ten children
options.B: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket supply costs
options.C: An absolute lack of any modern contraceptive methods globally
options.D: Laws that ban nurses from discussing birth control openly

explanation: Poverty and high out-of-pocket costs make access difficult, making knowledge of subsidized options vital for nurses. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What kind of tissue mainly lines the inside of your nose and sinus cavities?

options.A: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium
options.B: Non-ciliated transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple cuboidal glandular epithelium
options.D: Stratified squamous keratinized epithelium

explanation: Think of this lining as your nose's natural broom and filter system! It has tiny hair-like cilia and sticky mucus that trap dust and germs so they don't reach your lungs. You've got this!

question: Why should we teach caregivers how to spot danger signs when managing diarrhea at home?

options.A: So they can seek professional medical help before complications become life-threatening
options.B: So they can safely administer intravenous fluids at home
options.C: To eliminate the need for any further follow-up visits
options.D: To prevent family members from catching the same infection

explanation: Spotting warning signs early—like extreme drowsiness or blood in the stool—helps parents rush the child to the clinic before things turn critical.

question: Who acts as the central link for coordinating care between the patient and various medical specialists?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The patient's family
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: The pharmacist

explanation: As the nurse, you are the heartbeat of the ward! You coordinate the care plan and make sure information flows smoothly between everyone involved.

question: Why might a patient feel like they need to pass gas right after having a proctoscopy?

options.A: The enema fluid causes permanent irritation of the bowel
options.B: Dietary restrictions create excess gas in the stomach
options.C: Air is introduced into the rectum during the examination
options.D: Local anesthetics paralyze the internal sphincter muscles

explanation: That's right! The doctor pumps a little air into the bowel to see clearly, which naturally leaves the patient feeling a bit full or gassy afterward. It passes quickly!

question: What is an important thing to monitor after you take out a patient's catheter?

options.A: Insert a new catheter immediately to prevent infection
options.B: Monitor and document the patient's first spontaneous urination within 6 to 8 hours
options.C: Ensure the patient drinks at least five liters of water in the first hour
options.D: Check the patient's blood pressure every fifteen minutes

explanation: You're doing great! Watching for that first pee lets you know the bladder is waking back up and helps catch any post-removal retention early.

question: What is the primary goal of nursing care in an intensive care unit?

options.A: Discharging patients within twenty-four hours of admission
options.B: Replacing all mechanical equipment every shift
options.C: Administering the maximum dose of pain medication
options.D: Proactive prevention and early detection of complications

explanation: Critical care nursing centers on anticipating problems and catching tiny changes before they turn into full emergencies. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is a common pitfall parents fall into when a toddler's appetite drops?

options.A: Stopping all forms of milk consumption immediately
options.B: Giving the child adult-sized portions at every meal
options.C: Providing too many green leafy vegetables
options.D: Forcing food or offering constant sugary snacks

explanation: When toddlers eat less, worried parents sometimes force meals or hand over sugary snacks, which unfortunately leads to picky eating habits.

question: Why must speculums be either single-use plastic or properly sterilized metal?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients
options.B: To make the examination completely painless for everyone
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To ensure the equipment feels warm to the patient's touch

explanation: Spot on! Because these instruments touch mucous membranes, keeping them sterile or disposable stops bacteria and viruses from spreading from person to person.

question: Why can't steroid hormones be stored inside small cellular sacs (vesicles) before use?

options.A: They must be manufactured immediately by red blood cells
options.B: They are fat-soluble and easily diffuse right through cell membranes
options.C: They are too large to fit inside standard intracellular vesicles
options.D: They react violently with water stored inside cellular compartments

explanation: Because steroid hormones love fats, they slip right through cell walls like ghosts! That means cells can't trap them in little sacs—they just make them fresh whenever the body needs them.

question: What is a unique, tell-tale sign of fat embolism syndrome that sets it apart from other types of shock?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both lower extremities
options.B: Swelling of the fingers on the uninjured hand
options.C: A pinpoint petechiae rash across the chest and neck
options.D: A sudden drop in core body temperature

explanation: That distinctive pinprick red-purple rash (petechiae) on the chest and neck is a classic hallmark of fat emboli blocking tiny skin capillaries.

question: A wheelchair user visits the clinic complaining of unusual fatigue and constant thirst. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Investigate for potential systemic issues like diabetes
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to an orthotic specialist
options.C: Advise the patient to rest more and avoid further medical testing
options.D: Document that fatigue is a normal side effect of using a wheelchair

explanation: Never brush off new symptoms! Fatigue and thirst could mean something like diabetes, so they always deserve a proper check-up. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Nigerian staple foods like yam and cassava are famous for giving us a massive supply of which macronutrient?

options.A: Complete proteins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.C: Carbohydrates
options.D: Essential fatty acids

explanation: Exactly! Root crops and cereals like yam and cassava are our powerhouse sources of carbohydrates, giving our bodies the energy we need every day.

question: Why should a nurse explore a patient's cultural beliefs regarding traditional remedies and prescription drugs?

options.A: To understand the client's perspective and prevent dangerous drug interactions
options.B: To replace all doctor prescriptions with local herbs
options.C: To prove that modern hospital medicine is always superior
options.D: To avoid having to give injections during the shift

explanation: Patients often combine local herbs with prescription drugs. Knowing this helps nurses protect them from harmful drug reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which IV fluid is the ONLY one safe to use alongside blood products?

options.A: Ringer's Lactate Solution
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: Half-Normal Saline

explanation: Normal saline is isotonic and friendly to red blood cells, preventing them from bursting or clumping like other fluids might.

question: Why is it so important to quickly isolate a suspected Ebola patient in a clinic?

options.A: It allows the lab to make local drugs
options.B: It prevents the virus from spreading to other patients and healthcare staff
options.C: It eliminates the need to wear protective gowns
options.D: It cures the patient before bleeding starts

explanation: Spot on! Isolating patients cuts off the transmission chain immediately and keeps everyone else in the ward safe.

question: What happens to staff morale if hospital management uses MBO goals purely as a punitive tool?

options.A: Nurses become significantly more motivated to achieve higher targets
options.B: Patient satisfaction scores rise immediately due to strict rules
options.C: Administrative efficiency increases across all hospital departments
options.D: Staff feel anxious and view the process with fear rather than trust

explanation: Using goals to punish creates a toxic culture where staff hide mistakes instead of collaborating to fix them. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h6)

question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has long-term high blood pressure and is carrying twins. What should you, as her nurse, watch out for?

options.A: She has zero risk of complications because she is young.
options.B: She should stop all her blood pressure tablets right away.
options.C: She only needs normal, routine antenatal visits.
options.D: She needs closer monitoring for early signs of preeclampsia.

explanation: Having twins plus chronic high blood pressure puts her at a higher risk, so we need to keep a closer, caring eye on her throughout her pregnancy.

question: What actually happens during an in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure?

options.A: Sperm are placed directly into the uterus using a small catheter
options.B: Blocked fallopian tubes are surgically tied and opened
options.C: Eggs and sperm are fertilized together in a laboratory dish
options.D: Hormone injections are given to stop natural ovulation

explanation: With IVF, eggs are collected, mixed with sperm in a lab dish to fertilize, and the resulting embryo is placed into the uterus.

question: As a nurse, what is your absolute first priority when checking a patient who might have asphyxia?

options.A: Checking skin integrity over pressure points
options.B: Reviewing past medical and family history
options.C: Checking airway, breathing, and circulation
options.D: Measuring exact daily fluid intake and output

explanation: ABC comes first in every single emergency! Securing life-sustaining functions is always your top duty.

question: A patient with a back injury to the vertebrae has damage in which body cavity?

options.A: Thoracic cavity
options.B: Cranial cavity
options.C: Pelvic cavity
options.D: Spinal cavity

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cavity is enclosed by the backbone (vertebral column) and holds the delicate spinal cord.

question: On a CT scan, how does dense bone usually appear?

options.A: Pitch black
options.B: Bright white
options.C: Bright green
options.D: Transparent

explanation: Bone absorbs a lot of radiation, so it shows up as a bright white color on the image. You've got this!

question: How does a public health nurse's daily role differ from a nurse working on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Agency nurses never interact with actual human patients
options.B: Agency nurses focus on community-wide prevention rather than individual bedside treatment
options.C: Hospital nurses write all national healthcare laws
options.D: Agency nurses only dispense emergency medications

explanation: Well done! Ward nurses care for patients one-on-one at the bedside, while public health nurses look at whole communities and prevention strategies.

question: What is the main focus of manipulative and body-based therapies like massage?

options.A: The ingestion of raw botanical extracts
options.B: The manipulation of external spiritual energy fields
options.C: The physical structures and systems of the body
options.D: The psychological regulation of deep breathing

explanation: Well done! These therapies focus directly on working with the physical body parts, such as muscles and bones through massage or chiropractic care.

question: Why should patients take artemether-lumefantrine tablets with fatty food?

options.A: Fat neutralizes the bitter taste of the crushed tablets
options.B: Fat coats the stomach to completely prevent any nausea
options.C: Fat helps the kidneys excrete the drug much faster
options.D: Fat significantly improves the absorption of the lumefantrine component

explanation: Wonderful! Lumefantrine dissolves best in fat, so a fatty meal helps the body absorb it properly to knock out the malaria.

question: What is the main purpose of a survivorship care plan?

options.A: To manage acute surgical complications in the hospital
options.B: To replace the need for any further primary care visits
options.C: To guarantee that cancer will never return in the future
options.D: To outline treatment history and schedule ongoing surveillance

explanation: Think of it as a roadmap. A survivorship plan summarizes past treatments and maps out future health check-ups.

question: Where is the best place inside a refrigerator to store raw chicken breasts?

options.A: Inside the door racks
options.B: On the lowest shelf
options.C: On the top shelf
options.D: Next to fresh lettuce

explanation: Placing raw meat on the bottom shelf prevents blood and juices from dripping onto other foods that will not be cooked further. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h4)

question: What is the main goal of hospital antibiotic stewardship programs?

options.A: To encourage patients to take antibiotics for common colds
options.B: To ban all antibiotics from being stored in the country
options.C: To make expensive antibiotics available for free to staff
options.D: To promote the correct, rational use of antimicrobial drugs

explanation: Stewardship programs monitor and guide prescribing practices to prevent misuse and slow down antimicrobial resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is generally safe and does NOT harm sperm production?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Anabolic steroid abuse
options.C: Elevated scrotal temperature
options.D: Exposure to heavy toxins

explanation: Good news! Regular, moderate exercise keeps your body healthy and balanced. Heat, harsh toxins, and steroids, however, can hurt sperm counts.

question: Why is it smart to put a soft towel at the bottom of the sink when washing dentures?

options.A: To cushion them so they won't break if they slip and fall
options.B: To soak up extra water splashing onto your uniform
options.C: To give you a clean spot to put antiseptic cream
options.D: To keep metal pieces from scratching the shiny basin

explanation: Dentures are slippery when wet and expensive to replace! A padded sink saves the day if they accidentally drop from your hands.

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: To restrict patient access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical supervision in rural clinics
options.C: To track service quality, identify gaps, and guide continuous improvement
options.D: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors in patient charts

explanation: You're doing great! Monitoring collects essential data so managers can improve care delivery and patient safety.

question: What is the primary role of glucagon during a fasting state?

options.A: To signal the liver to release stored glucose into the blood
options.B: To help the pancreas produce more beta cells for energy
options.C: To block insulin from entering the muscle tissues
options.D: To transport excess sugar directly to the kidneys for excretion

explanation: When fasting lowers blood sugar, glucagon tells the liver to break down stored glycogen to keep blood sugar from dropping too low. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h2)

question: What happens when health workers make promises to a community and fail to keep them?

options.A: Local leaders take over nursing duties
options.B: The community becomes more eager to help
options.C: Government funding increases automatically
options.D: Trust is broken, leading to poor cooperation

explanation: Broken promises destroy trust, making future health initiatives extremely difficult to implement. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h6)

question: How does confusion or memory loss directly increase a patient's safety risk?

options.A: It causes the ward floors to become slippery
options.B: It makes it hard for the patient to understand safety instructions
options.C: It directly lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It prevents medications from being absorbed properly

explanation: Patients with memory or thinking problems often forget their limits (like needing help to walk), which can lead to falls. Always good to keep an extra eye on them!

question: Which part of the anal sphincter mechanism is under voluntary control?

options.A: Internal anal sphincter
options.B: Hemorrhoidal vascular plexus
options.C: External anal sphincter
options.D: Sigmoidal smooth muscle

explanation: The external anal sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, allowing conscious control to tighten the anus and prevent leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why must nurses look beyond vital signs when assessing a patient?

options.A: Doctors handle physical assessments while nurses only do paperwork
options.B: Physical numbers do not show how the patient emotionally experiences the disease
options.C: Vital signs are completely useless in clinical nursing practice
options.D: Patients never tell the truth about their physical pain levels

explanation: Vital signs tell us about the body, but talking to the patient tells us about their fears, coping skills, and emotional state.

question: What is the main job of the three tiny bones in the middle ear?

options.A: Produce cerumen to trap foreign bodies
options.B: Amplify and transmit sound vibrations
options.C: Drain excess fluid from the inner ear
options.D: Maintain balance and body posture

explanation: Meet the malleus, incus, and stapes! They take the vibrations from your eardrum, boost their volume, and pass them deeper into the ear.

question: What is a very common cause of esophageal strictures (narrowing) that need dilation?

options.A: Chronic acid reflux disease
options.B: Benign gastric hypersecretion
options.C: Excessive dietary fiber intake
options.D: Congenital throat widening

explanation: When stomach acid keeps splashing up into the esophagus over a long time, it irritates the tissue, causes scarring, and makes the passage narrow.

question: Which supplement is given to pregnant women to help prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Zinc gluconate
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Folic acid is a super important vitamin during early pregnancy. It helps the baby's brain and spinal cord develop properly.

question: What is Murphy's sign used to check for during a physical exam?

options.A: Pancreatitis
options.B: Cholecystitis
options.C: Appendicitis
options.D: Splenomegaly

explanation: Spot on! Murphy's sign is a classic way doctors and nurses check for gallbladder inflammation by pressing gently on the right upper belly while the patient takes a deep breath.

question: Who typically leads a peer-led HIV support group?

options.A: A licensed medical doctor or surgeon
options.B: A hospital laboratory technician
options.C: A veteran community member living with HIV
options.D: A government health policy maker

explanation: Peer-led groups are guided by individuals who share the lived experience of managing the condition successfully. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: What factor makes the emotional and mental distress much worse for patients recovering from an unsafe abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Social stigma and fear of legal consequences
options.B: Excessive availability of professional counselors
options.C: Mandatory psychological screening in government hospitals
options.D: Immediate support from community religious leaders

explanation: Fear of being arrested, judged, or rejected by loved ones forces many women to hide their pain and suffer all alone. As nurses, being a safe, listening ear makes all the difference.

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why central nervous system neurons struggle to repair themselves?

options.A: Schwann cells create perfect guiding tubes for repair
options.B: Oligodendrocytes fail to form functional repair tracts
options.C: Growth-inhibiting molecules block axonal sprouts
options.D: Astrocytes form physical scar tissue blocks

explanation: Schwann cells actually help nerves heal, but they live in the *peripheral* nervous system, not the central nervous system. The CNS lacks this helpful environment!

question: What happens in the colon when someone doesn't drink enough water?

options.A: Peristalsis becomes dangerously fast and watery
options.B: Gastric acid production increases rapidly
options.C: The colon extracts more water, causing hard and dry stool
options.D: The colon stops absorbing nutrients completely

explanation: When the body is short on water, the colon tries to save every drop by sucking extra moisture out of the waste, leading to dry, hard stools.

question: A patient has severe laryngitis with a painful, raspy voice and is given steam inhalation. What is the main goal here?

options.A: To deliver systemic antibiotics directly into the bloodstream
options.B: To force deep lung expansion in the lower alveoli
options.C: To soothe inflamed vocal cords and mucosal tissues
options.D: To permanently cure the viral infection overnight

explanation: You got it! Moist heat hydrates dry, raw throat tissues, taking away that scratchy irritation and giving sore vocal cords a chance to rest and heal.

question: What is the most common mild side effect patients report when taking oral expectorants?

options.A: Nausea and gastrointestinal upset
options.B: Sudden loss of color vision
options.C: Permanent hearing loss in both ears
options.D: Severe high blood pressure spikes

explanation: Spot on. Because these drugs work by slightly irritating the stomach lining, mild tummy upset or nausea can sometimes happen.

question: Why do oral medications have to pass through the liver before reaching the rest of the body?

options.A: The liver is the primary site where red blood cells absorb the drug
options.B: Stomach acid forces the drug directly into the bile ducts
options.C: Bile salts are required to activate every type of oral pill
options.D: Hepatic first-pass metabolism alters or breaks down part of the drug

explanation: This is known as the 'first-pass effect'! Blood from your gut goes straight to the liver via the portal vein, where liver enzymes get the first chance to process or break down a portion of the drug.

question: What is usually the very first step when starting a management audit?

options.A: Dismissing the hospital management board
options.B: Writing the final punishment list for failing staff
options.C: Conducting a preliminary survey to gather background information
options.D: Publicly advertising audit results in local newspapers

explanation: Auditors never just dive in blindly! They start with a preliminary survey to get familiar with the environment and layout before doing any deep investigation.

question: What is a major reason why Nigeria is facing a shortage of skilled nurses right now?

options.A: A complete ban on private nursing practice
options.B: The mass migration of healthcare professionals abroad
options.C: Mandatory retirement at age thirty
options.D: The total closure of all nursing training institutions

explanation: Spot on. Many skilled nurses are travelling abroad for better opportunities, leaving a big gap at home.

question: For a first-time mother in active labour, how fast should the cervix open?

options.A: Half a centimetre every two hours
options.B: At least one centimetre per hour
options.C: Two centimetres every thirty minutes
options.D: Three centimetres per hour

explanation: Good job! Once active labour is well underway, we expect the cervix to dilate by a minimum of one centimetre every hour.

question: A nurse is teaching a patient with poor leg circulation about foot care. Which tip is the most important to include?

options.A: Walk barefoot around the house to toughen your soles
options.B: Soak your feet in warm water for an hour every night
options.C: Check your feet every day for cuts, redness, or blisters
options.D: Cut your toenails into rounded corners with deep edges

explanation: Because poor blood flow slows down healing, even a tiny scratch can turn into a stubborn sore. Daily checks help catch small issues early!

question: Which receptors detect a sudden drop in blood pressure during a haemorrhage?

options.A: Pain receptors
options.B: Chemoreceptors
options.C: Baroreceptors
options.D: Thermoreceptors

explanation: Baroreceptors are pressure sensors located in major blood vessels that notice when blood pressure falls and alert the nervous system. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which traditional method uses heat from the sun to remove moisture from crops?

options.A: Refrigeration
options.B: Sun-drying
options.C: Irradiation
options.D: Pasteurization

explanation: Sun-drying is a classic, natural method using solar heat and fresh air to dry out things like grains and peppers.

question: Which needle size and length is standard for an adult intramuscular injection?

options.A: 25 gauge, 1/2 inch needle
options.B: 27 gauge, 3/8 inch needle
options.C: 22 gauge, 1.5 inch needle
options.D: 31 gauge, 5/8 inch needle

explanation: You need a longer needle and a wider opening (like a 22-gauge, 1.5-inch) to bypass skin and fat and reach deep down into adult muscle tissue.

question: A nurse checks if a school handwashing campaign successfully reduced diarrhea cases over the term. What kind of evaluation is this?

options.A: Summative evaluation
options.B: Formative evaluation
options.C: Financial audit
options.D: Administrative assessment

explanation: Summative evaluation looks at the final results and overall impact after the whole educational program has wrapped up.

question: Which organs take the biggest hit from long-term iron overload caused by frequent blood transfusions?

options.A: Lungs, pleura, and upper airways
options.B: Brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves
options.C: Liver, heart, and endocrine glands
options.D: Stomach, intestines, and pancreas

explanation: Extra iron loves to settle down in hard-working organs like the liver, the heart muscle, and hormone-making glands, eventually causing tissue damage if not treated.

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

options.A: Identify hypertension as a contraindication and discuss safer alternative methods
options.B: Prescribe the pills immediately because blood pressure does not matter
options.C: Refuse to check the client's blood pressure during the visit
options.D: Tell the client that birth control pills cure high blood pressure

explanation: Estrogen-containing pills can worsen high blood pressure and increase stroke risk, so nurses must screen for medical conditions and offer safer choices like progestin-only options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: What defines an orphan drug?

options.A: A medication developed to treat a rare medical condition
options.B: An herbal supplement with no scientific research backing
options.C: A controlled substance classified under Schedule I rules
options.D: A drug that has been abandoned by the manufacturing company

explanation: Orphan drugs are specifically created to help patients suffering from rare diseases that affect few people. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe injection practice?

options.A: Reusing a disposable syringe after washing it with warm water
options.B: Disposing of used needles immediately into a puncture-proof box
options.C: Using a brand new, sterile syringe for every single patient
options.D: Wiping the rubber top of a medication vial with an alcohol swab

explanation: Never wash and reuse disposable syringes! Washing doesn't kill microscopic germs. Every patient deserves a fresh, sterile syringe.

question: How does carrying extra body weight affect weight-bearing joints like the knees?

options.A: By drying out the synovial fluid completely
options.B: By stopping blood flow to the bone marrow
options.C: By increasing chemical toxins in the blood
options.D: By placing continuous mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints

explanation: Well done! Extra weight means extra physical pressure on joints like your knees and hips with every single step you take.

question: Which intra-operative nursing role operates within the sterile field and handles surgical instruments directly?

options.A: Circulating nurse
options.B: Anesthetic nurse
options.C: Scrub nurse
options.D: Recovery room nurse

explanation: The scrub nurse dons sterile gowns and gloves to work directly next to the surgeon, managing instruments and maintaining the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a great community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Arresting family members immediately upon hearing rumors
options.B: Ignoring cultural beliefs and focusing strictly on hospital rules
options.C: Promoting alternative rites of passage that do not involve cutting
options.D: Training traditional practitioners to use sterile razor blades

explanation: Communities love celebrating their youth growing up! By supporting non-cutting ceremonies, we respect the culture while keeping our girls safe.

question: What does the presence of bacteria on a synovial fluid Gram stain indicate?

options.A: Septic arthritis
options.B: Normal joint aging
options.C: Simple osteoarthritis
options.D: Mild muscle fatigue

explanation: Bacteria in the joint space signify a severe joint infection requiring urgent antibiotic treatment. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h6)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient gets a chemical splashed into both eyes?

options.A: Flush the eyes continuously with clean water or normal saline for at least fifteen minutes
options.B: Rub the eyes firmly with a dry towel to remove solid particles
options.C: Put neutral cooking oil directly into the eyes to coat the chemical
options.D: Apply tight gauze patches over both eyes and wait for an ophthalmologist

explanation: Water is your best friend here! Long, continuous flushing washes away caustic chemicals before they can damage the cornea.

question: Why should a recovering hyperemesis patient avoid drinking lots of fluid during meals?

options.A: It permanently ruins the function of the kidneys
options.B: It stretches the stomach quickly and can trigger vomiting
options.C: It washes away all the digestive enzymes in the mouth
options.D: It causes severe cramping in the lower extremities

explanation: Chugging water alongside food overfills the stomach too fast, which is an express ticket right back to vomiting. Small sips separate from meals are best!

question: What must a unit manager consider when making a fair duty roster?

options.A: Patient acuity and staff skill mix
options.B: The distance of each nurse's house from the hospital
options.C: The personal fashion preferences of nurses
options.D: Only the seniority of the nurses

explanation: Exactly! A good roster looks at how sick the patients are (acuity) and matches them with nurses who have the right skills for the job.

question: In public health, what term is commonly used instead of 'accident' for injuries that happen without bad intentions?

options.A: Intentional injuries
options.B: Unintentional injuries
options.C: Spontaneous trauma
options.D: Stochastic events

explanation: Great job! Public health experts prefer 'unintentional injuries' because most events we call accidents can actually be predicted and prevented.

question: Which part of the retina helps us see sharp, colorful images in bright light?

options.A: Cones
options.B: Cornea
options.C: Lens
options.D: Rods

explanation: You can remember 'Cones for Color'! Cones are the hardworking cells in our eyes that give us clear details and vibrant colors when the lights are bright.

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily after an unsafe abortion. What action should you take right away?

options.A: Perform a complete pelvic exam without checking vital signs
options.B: Start a large-bore intravenous line for fluid resuscitation
options.C: Ask the patient to write down a detailed confession of the act
options.D: Wait for the attending physician to arrive before acting

explanation: You got this! When someone is bleeding heavily, getting IV access fast is crucial to restore fluids, boost blood volume, and prevent shock.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the direct link between the nervous system and the endocrine system?

options.A: Thalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master bridge! It takes nervous system signals and translates them into hormonal commands for the pituitary gland.

question: Which tool is used to hold the surgical needle securely when repairing an episiotomy?

options.A: Needle holder
options.B: Mucus extractor
options.C: Anatomical fetoscope
options.D: Cord scissors

explanation: A needle holder gives you a firm, non-slip grip so you can pass your stitches smoothly and comfortably.

question: Which body language shows a supportive and comforting style to a nervous patient?

options.A: Standing over the bed to show clinical dominance
options.B: Staring intently at the medical chart while the patient speaks
options.C: Crossing arms firmly across the chest to establish authority
options.D: Maintaining a calm tone and open, welcoming body language

explanation: A gentle voice and open posture tell the patient 'I am here for you, and you are safe with me.'

question: What is the typical length of a normal adult fallopian tube?

options.A: 20 to 25 centimeters
options.B: 15 to 20 centimeters
options.C: 7 to 14 centimeters
options.D: 2 to 4 centimeters

explanation: Normal fallopian tubes measure about 7 to 14 centimeters long, which is the perfect size to catch and transport eggs safely.

question: What is the main reason clinical instructors use direct observation?

options.A: Measuring patient satisfaction scores
options.B: Evaluating a student's personal writing style
options.C: Testing theoretical knowledge of disease pathology
options.D: Assessing psychomotor skills and clinical performance

explanation: Watching you perform a procedure hands-on is the best way to see how well you apply your practical nursing skills.

question: What is a major duty of a nurse working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Living with families to supervise their daily meal preparation
options.B: Building local community infrastructure and public roads
options.C: Acting as a direct caregiver and monitor of acute treatments
options.D: Operating primary health clinics without physician oversight

explanation: Right on! Hospital nurses spend their shifts giving hands-on care, giving meds, and keeping a close eye on acutely ill patients.

question: Which part of the eye is damaged in all types of glaucoma?

options.A: The outer cornea
options.B: The crystalline lens
options.C: The optic nerve
options.D: The white of the eye

explanation: Glaucoma is all about pressure or stress hurting the optic nerve fibers, which slowly creates blind spots if left untreated.

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for someone living with HIV?

options.A: Suppressing the viral load and protecting immune function
options.B: Stimulating the immediate production of thick mucosal barriers
options.C: Permanently killing all virus particles within the bone marrow
options.D: Preventing the development of seasonal respiratory allergies

explanation: Spot on! ART keeps the virus levels super low, which keeps the immune system strong and healthy.

question: What colour and flow pattern does arterial bleeding typically show?

options.A: Bright red and trickling evenly
options.B: Bright red and spurting in jets
options.C: Dark red and oozing slowly
options.D: Dark red and flowing in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure from the heart, causing it to spurt out in pulses when a vessel is cut. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h1)

question: Which type of synovial joint gives you the biggest range of movement in all directions?

options.A: Hinge joint
options.B: Pivot joint
options.C: Plane joint
options.D: Ball-and-socket joint

explanation: That's right! Your shoulders and hips are ball-and-socket joints, allowing you to swing your arms and legs in almost any direction.

question: Why do our hands and lips take up so much more space in the brain's sensory map than our back?

options.A: They have thicker layers of subcutaneous fat
options.B: They are located closer to the brain
options.C: They receive a larger volume of arterial blood
options.D: They possess a much higher density of touch receptors

explanation: Makes sense, right? We use our hands and lips for detailed tasks, so they need way more brain power and receptor coverage than our backs!

question: How do Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) stop HIV from multiplying?

options.A: By destroying red blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By preventing viral DNA from inserting into the host cell's DNA
options.C: By changing the patient's blood type permanently
options.D: By blocking the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: You got it! INSTIs block the 'integrase' enzyme, which the virus uses like glue to paste its own genetic code into our human cells.

question: What term describes community protection that happens when a large percentage of people become immune to a disease?

options.A: Herd immunity
options.B: Cellular immunity
options.C: Passive immunity
options.D: Active immunity

explanation: That's herd immunity! When most of the community is protected, it builds a shield that guards the babies and vulnerable people who can't get vaccinated yet.
